clue.text: One's bedded down in wagon-lit

definitions.meaning: a railway tie, the timber beam bedded down in the ballast under the rails
French for a railway carriage with berths, a night-train sleeping car

explanation.surface: Someone tucked up for the night in a continental sleeping carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: the beam laid beneath railway track, and the train carriage with beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard dictionary meanings: a track beam set into ballast, and a sleeping car on a train.

clue.text: Spooner acclaims Mia's role in Zulu Dawn

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of the phrase is wanted

parts.note: the actress Mia Farrow, so her surname with the possessive
a role is a part an actor plays

explanation.surface: An actress's part in the film Zulu Dawn is being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, "Farrow's part" runs as "Farrow spart"; swapping the F and SP sounds gives the slang term. SPARROWFART is jocular British slang for the crack of dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular British slang for first light, when the small birds wake up.

clue.text: Entice Mr Clooney to use Western Union?

indicators.note: to use the letters is to make something new out of them, rearranging them freely

explanation.surface: Tempting George Clooney into sending funds through a money-transfer firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' signals rearranging ENTICEMRCLOONEY. Western Union is a famous money-transfer company; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Union transfers are an instance of funds sent by wire rather than as cash, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Parking places for lorry drivers to tuck in over men's magazines

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: tucking something in puts it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: lay-bys are roadside stopping places where British lorry drivers pull in
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Truckers in roadside lay-bys tucking into girlie magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside pull-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is a famous title among top-shelf magazines aimed at men, so the plural names such publications.

clue.text: Germany probes unagi sashimi reportedly not "fair trade"

indicators.note: something that probes goes inside, so one piece is put into the other
says the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: unagi is Japanese for freshwater eel, and sashimi is served uncooked
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German poking at Japanese raw fish and finding it not ethically sourced.
explanation.walkthrough: Unagi is Japanese freshwater eel and sashimi is served uncooked; 'reportedly' gives the sound of the eel phrase, and 'probes' sets Germany's code within.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment is the idiom's meaning, the opposite of a fair bargain.

clue.text: Virgin Radio broadcast tracked down

indicators.note: anything heard over the airwaves is heard, not read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: chased means pursued or hunted down

explanation.surface: A station on Virgin Radio has been located.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin Radio is a British radio station, so 'Virgin' looks like part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A virgin is sexually pure, abstaining from intercourse; used adjectivally it is a synonym.

clue.text: What's up? Labour's 2015 dream team paid attention

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what was said
Ed Miliband and Ed Balls, the Labour leader and shadow chancellor at the 2015 UK election

explanation.surface: Asking what is going on, then noting that Labour's 2015 leading pair were listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2015 Britain's Labour Party was led by Ed Miliband with Ed Balls as shadow chancellor: two Eds.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of advice, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Petty criminals conceal trafficked Timor coke in underwear

indicators.note: to conceal something in a place is to hide it inside, so the one piece wraps the other

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underclothes

indicators.note: drugs that are trafficked are moved about, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Low-level crooks stuff smuggled East Timorese cocaine in their knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear; 'trafficked' signals the anagram and 'conceal' the container. Small Time Crooks is a Woody Allen film.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor lawbreakers are described as operating on a small scale; it is also a Woody Allen film title.

clue.text: Very few regularly watch

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone keeps an eye out on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of VERYFEW are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to keep under observation, a synonym of look at closely.

clue.text: I'm told Liam will feature up front for The Mariners

definitions.text: feature up front for The Mariners

indicators.note: hearsay, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: Liam Fox, the British Conservative politician, contracted with will gives Fox'll

explanation.surface: Word is a player called Liam will start as striker for Grimsby Town, nicknamed The Mariners.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Fox is a British Conservative MP; "Fox'll" is said just like the contracted spelling of forecastle.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the raised deck at a ship's bow, part of the vessel that sailors know.

clue.text: Gunners failing to finish second, missing the Emirates?

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so this letter is taken away
the word stops short, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: the Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal football club

explanation.surface: Arsenal miss out on runner-up spot, not playing at their home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emirates Stadium is Arsenal's home ground in London, so the definition hides in the club's own story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emirates is a stadium, an example of a venue for sport, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Extensive cheers in Toledo as Jonah is found

indicators.note: the cheers sit the way Jonah sits: inside the creature that swallowed him

parts.note: the Bible's Jonah is found in the belly of the whale
ole is the Spanish cry of approval, Toledo being a Spanish city

explanation.surface: Shouts of Spanish approval are widespread where a biblical prophet turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonah was swallowed by a great fish, usually called a whale, so 'as Jonah is found' means placed inside WHALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale changes are sweeping and broad in scope, a common figurative sense.

clue.text: Italian island sailor heading west likely to get tax demand

indicators.note: in an across clue westward is right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled
tar is an old slang word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman sailing west from Elba expects a bill from the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' reads ELBATAR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that is rateable is liable to local rates, a British property tax.

clue.text: Add gloss to finale of Annie Hall, shot in South Carolina

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters within the state abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for the US state

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so these letters are rearranged
the finale is the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Polishing the closing scene of Woody Allen's Annie Hall, filmed in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges EHALL into HELLA, which goes 'in' SC.
explanation.definitionFit: To shellac is to varnish with a resin lacquer, giving a glossy finish.

clue.text: Eco-city, safe resort for the chattering classes

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A green, secure town makes a holiday destination for chattering liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means sort again. Cafe Society is a Woody Allen film.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable people who gather in smart restaurants and talk, a near synonym for the opinionated elite.

clue.text: Visiting Hollywood, y'all? Enjoy his work here!

definitions.text: Visiting Hollywood, y'all? Enjoy his work here!

indicators.note: a visitor is only temporarily inside, so the name lies within these words

explanation.surface: A cheerful American greeting to tourists coming to Tinseltown.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs through hollyWOOD Y'ALL ENjoy, and the puzzle itself holds several of his film titles to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The film-maker's work appears throughout this grid, so the whole clue points to him.

clue.text: Leaves note, leading to row

indicators.note: says one piece comes first and the other follows

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
ff. is the abbreviation for folios, the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: Someone walks out, leaving a note, and that sparks a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is pages: ff is the abbreviation for following pages or folios.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, the sense of row that rhymes with cow.

clue.text: Most murky coastal fog enveloping Spain

indicators.note: wrapping round, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a sea mist is fog rolling in from the sea
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A sea fog shrouding the Spanish coast is at its thickest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murky' looks like weather but means shady or sordid.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamy means sordid or disreputable, so the superlative is the shadiest.

clue.text: Related to becoming aroused, naked?

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: waking means coming round from sleep

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether arousal and nudity go together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips the outer W and G from WAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things of a similar kind are said to be kindred or similar, used with to.

clue.text: Band of Brothers?

parts.note: reads as the war drama, but it is a pop group made up of the Gibb brothers

explanation.surface: The title of a famous wartime drama series.
explanation.walkthrough: The pop trio were the brothers Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical group whose members were siblings, quite literally a band of brothers.

clue.text: Try on Eliot's suit

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the other piece

parts.note: a judge hears a case when trying it
T. S. Eliot, the poet, by his initials

explanation.surface: Someone tries on a suit belonging to Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four card suits in a deck, alongside clubs, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Crazy grandma in revolting Swedish car

indicators.note: puts one piece inside the other
turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Saab is a Swedish car maker
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny in a disgusting old Swedish car has lost her marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns SAAB into BAAS, with NAN placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is slang for going mad, so it means insane or wild.

clue.text: Have only one pill and some lighter fluid

parts.note: but means merely, as in 'but a child'
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Take just one tablet along with a squirt of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Butane is the liquefied gas used to fuel cigarette lighters, one of several such fuels.

clue.text: Almost time for original, American deep-fried food

indicators.note: nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tempo is the time or speed of music
ur- is a prefix meaning original or earliest

explanation.surface: It's nearly time for authentic American fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts TEMPO to TEMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables coated in light batter and fried in hot oil.

clue.text: Hesitate twice to enter social security premiums digitally

definitions.note: an adverb, but it defines an adjective meaning in digits

indicators.note: going in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: NIC stands for National Insurance contributions, the British social security payments
um and er are two sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over paying social security contributions online.
explanation.walkthrough: National Insurance contributions are Britain's social security payments; 'to enter' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeric means expressed in figures, which is what digital means in its basic sense.

clue.text: Island cocktail

definitions.meaning: the island at the heart of New York City
a mixed drink of whiskey, vermouth and bitters

explanation.walkthrough: It is also a Woody Allen film.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the New York borough on its island, and the classic whiskey and vermouth drink.

clue.text: It's maliciously slung by toaster into 8

definitions.meaning: insults and smears are thrown at opponents in a dirty campaign
the drinking toast 'Here's ... in your eye', 8 being the answer to 8 Down

explanation.surface: Something thrown into someone's eye by a person raising a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toaster' is one proposing a toast, not a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud-slinging is smearing a reputation, and the old toast is 'here's mud in your eye'.

clue.text: Run off with lady responsible for Parker pen theft

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so these letters go

parts.note: Lady Penelope in Thunderbirds employs Parker as her chauffeur
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes off with a lady's fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Thunderbirds is a British puppet TV series in which Lady Penelope has a chauffeur called Parker; Parker is also a pen brand, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off to marry in secret, usually with a lover, is the classic sense.

clue.text: Retire exhausted, taking Times to relax here?

definitions.note: a description of a place, standing for a noun

indicators.note: retiring is going back, so the letters are read backwards
taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: dead tired, worn out
by means multiplied by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Go to bed worn out, taking a newspaper along to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplied by; 'taking' signals the container and 'Retire' reverses the whole, giving the letters DEBYAD read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A daybed is a couch for lounging on in the daytime, a place for resting.

clue.text: Please shut up Mick Jagger!

definitions.meaning: to please is to gratify or content someone
Jagger complains he can't get no satisfaction, so granting it would silence him

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for the Rolling Stones' singer to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rolling Stones song is (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone fully, the verb behind the noun of the Stones hit.
